theme_central: Comparison between grateful kings (Dawud, Sulayman) and the ungrateful kingdom of Sheba, destroyed despite its opulence — true power comes from gratitude, not possession.
sources_note: Well-sourced structure (grokipedia): the kingdom of Sheba (15-21) strategically placed between the narrative of the grateful kings and the warnings addressed to the Meccans.

branches.title: Opening
branches.resume: Praise to Allah, owner of everything, knowing even the weight of an atom; refutation of doubt about the Hour.

children.t: Praise to Allah, absolute omniscience, refutation of doubt about the Hour

branches.title: Dawud and Sulayman, grateful kings
branches.resume: Mountains and birds glorifying with Dawud, wind and jinn subdued to Sulayman.

children.t: Dawud: mountains and birds glorifying with him, iron made soft
Sulayman: wind and jinn subdued, his death discovered by a worm eating through his staff

branches.title: The kingdom of Sheba
branches.resume: Source of the surah's name: the two gardens, the broken dam, dispersal of the ungrateful people.

children.t: The two gardens of Sheba, dam broken because of ingratitude
Dispersal of the people, trial of free choice confirmed

branches.title: Refutation of the idols, universal mission
branches.resume: The idols own nothing, share nothing with Allah; Muhammad sent to all mankind.

children.t: Refutation of the idols, unable to own anything at all
Muhammad sent to all mankind, question about the timing of the Hour

branches.title: Debate weak/arrogant, sustenance
branches.resume: Mutual rejection of responsibility in Hell, sustenance broadened or restricted according to divine wisdom.

children.t: Debate between the weak and the arrogant in Hell, mutual rejection of responsibility
The wealthy the first to reject the messengers; sustenance according to divine wisdom

branches.title: Refutation, call to reflect
branches.resume: Accusation of sorcery refuted, previous mightier generations destroyed, too late in the face of punishment.

children.t: Accusation of sorcery refuted, previous mightier generations destroyed
Call to reflect calmly, too late to believe at the moment of punishment
